title: Roll five dice from a felt-lined dice cup into a folding dice tray, then stand the cup back on the table
keywords: loose parts in a held container
instruction: Roll the five dice from the cup into the dice tray, then put the cup back down on the table.
context: A Yahtzee turn begins by rolling all five dice from the shaker cup. The cup is round, light and open: it has to be held by its side and turned mouth-down high enough over a small tray that all five dice fall out together and tumble, yet none bounce out over its 3 cm walls. Tipped low and slowly, the dice just slide out; turned too little, they stay in the felt.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), measured on the table top. (1) Folding dice tray, snapped up, lying flat (taped down): PU leather walls 0.6 cm thick and 3.2 cm tall, velvet floor 0.4 cm thick, outside 15.2 cm (x) by 22.9 cm (y), centred at x 28.5, y 6.5. (2) Dice cup, upright, centred at x 30.0, y -17.0: felt-lined stitched leather over a plastic shell, red felt inside, 8.3 cm across, 9.5 cm tall, 0.3 cm wall, 0.4 cm base, 80 g. (3) Five opaque 16 mm six-sided acrylic dice with white pips, rounded corners, 4.5 g each, one each green, pink, black, blue and red, in one layer on the cup floor: four in a square at x +-0.95, y +-0.95 cm from the cup's centre (3 mm apart) and the fifth at x -2.8, y 0; faces along x and y; tops 1, 3, 5, 6 and 4 in that order (square: front-left, back-left, front-right, back-right, where front is +x and left is +y; then the fifth). The five colors uniquely identify the dice in a 240 fps real-trial video. Distractors, ignored by the scorer: (4) a score pad (paper notebook, 22.9 x 17.0 x 1.0 cm, 120 g) at x 17, y 30, long side along x; (5) a ceramic mug (11.4 x 9.0 x 8.0 cm, 300 g) at x 43, y 25; (6) a glass tumbler (8.0 cm across, 8.5 cm tall, 250 g) at x 45, y -17. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: A die counts when all hold: (a) its centre first leaves the cup interior (above the rim plane or outside the wall), then a different number becomes its upper-facing face at least once before it settles; (b) no gripper finger touched it at any time; (c) at the end it lies flat on one face on the tray floor (lowest point within 3 mm of the floor, a face within 8 deg of level, not leaning on a wall or another die) inside the walls, still (under 1 cm/s). The cup is set down when it stands upright (within 10 deg) on the table, wholly outside the tray, with every gripper finger 3 cm or more away, still. Score: 0 dice count: 0; 1 or 2: 0.25; 3 or 4: 0.5; all 5: 0.75; all 5 and the cup set down, held 3 s: 1.0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: an oblique 240 fps video identifies each colored die and shows its upper-facing pips after it exits and before it settles; the same video shows finger contact; an overhead end photo checks the die and cup poses.
reset_notes: Put the five dice back in the cup in the starting layout (tops 1, 3, 5, 6, 4) and stand the cup on its taped circle; the tray stays taped down.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Dice are 16 mm chamfered cubes (one convex collider each), pips drawn on. The cup is a 24-panel wall on a disc base, felt drawn on. The tray is fixed boxes; its velvet and padding do not deform. Friction (static/dynamic, estimates): dice 0.40/0.35, tray 0.50/0.45, cup 0.80/0.70. Restitution (estimates): dice 0.35, tray 0.20, cup 0.10. Distractors are SimReady props.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper reached the cup and moved around it, but never lifted or turned it; no die left the cup); demo: 1.0
